source.title: Prelude in C♯ minor, Op. 3 No. 2

bars.description: Play the pickup, then printed bars 1–61 once; returns are written out, with no inserted repeat.

endpoints.basis: The first A-octave attack is near 1.22 s. The broad final search selected the penultimate upper chord near 217.8 s, not the visibly distinct final pianissimo reattack near 220.4 s. Both repeated upper chords must remain represented.

anchors.label: coda-second-chord-A-sharp3-G-sharp4-signature
anchors.basis: The source's changed A-sharp3/G-sharp4 combination peaks near197.76s. It is the second coda voicing, not a delayed first chord or an interchangeable tonic-pedal onset.

anchors.label: coda-third-chord-G3-A4-signature

anchors.basis: The fourth voicing has F-sharp3/A-sharp3/F-sharp4/A-sharp4 near206.38s. Preserve its order and chromatic change rather than matching a neighbouring bass attack.

anchors.label: coda-fifth-chord-D-sharp-F-sharp-A-signature
anchors.basis: The fifth chord's D-sharp/F-sharp/A signature is visible near211.50s in logarithmic absolute-pitch features, before the separate low C-sharp-minor closing voicing.

anchors.label: closing-lower-C-sharp-minor-voicing
anchors.basis: The lower closing voicing's G-sharp3/G-sharp4 pair peaks near215.12s, before the higher penultimate chord at217.6s and its final reattack. The weak historic signal is inspected fitting evidence, not an aural or independent check.

anchors.label: penultimate-upper-C-sharp-minor-chord
anchors.basis: The written eighth-note upper chord at q241.5 is reattacked as the final fermata chord at q242. Inspection distinguishes the stronger earlier attack near 217.8 s from the later pianissimo repeat near 220.4 s; the old endpoint had conflated them. This explicit fitting constraint is not independent or aural validation.
